::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 23d 1865  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 69-70
:::

My dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd),
I think I ought to refer to you a request I have had from Dr and Mrs Vaughan[^1] for leave to put two of the stories in [Golden Deeds](cmy_books/cmybook_51.qmd) i.e. 'The last fight in the Colyseum', and the faithful slaves of Haïti into a [An Advanced Reading Book for Girls](other_books/otherbook_392.qmd)book of readings] for National Schools acknowledging where they come from, but I conclude that you have no objection. When there is a reprint, I have another faithful slave to put in who maintained his mistress by hair dressing in New York.

Thank you for the [Clever Woman](cmy_books/cmybook_58.qmd)’s arrival. She looks very well and attractive, but I am prepared for all the critics doubting her reformation

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Probably the Rev. [Charles John Vaughan](people/person_1439.qmd) (1816-1897), vicar of Doncaster and former headmaster of Harrow School, and his wife Catherine Maria (Stanley) Vaughan (1821-1899). Mrs Vaughan edited *An Advanced Reading Book for Girls* (1866).
